newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Inter-Tajik peace talks open in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Inter-Tajik peace talks open in Moscow.

text.p: Tajik government representatives and their Islamist opponents started a round of talks in Moscow on Wednesday aimed at working out military details of a peace accord agreed last December.

"We have come to Moscow with a firm intention of resolving the package of military issues," Russian news agencies quoted Talbak Nazarov, Tajikistan's foreign minister, as saying before the start of the talks.
The talks are mediated by Russia, which keeps a large military presence in the former Soviet republic of 5.7 million people.

The Moscow-backed Tajik government and Islamic opposition, based mostly in Afghanistan after a defeat in a four-year civil war, signed a ceasefire agreement in Iran last December which appears to be holding unlike previous truces.
But Western observers in the impoverished Central Asian republic say the two sides' inability to control armed bands who roam the mountain state may jeopardise peace efforts.

Diplomats say a power-sharing deal struck in Iran last week, in which seats on a new commission for national reconciliation were shared out between the government and opposition, could be explosive because it leaves no places for any other faction.
The commission, to be chaired by opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri, is to implement the U.N.-sponsored peace accord. Beleaguered President Imomali Rakhmonov stays in his post.
The Moscow round of talks is likely to centre on how to incorporate armed units of the opposition into the Tajik army. It was not immediately clear how long the talks would last.
